hero.headline: Trump tells Netanyahu not to retaliate after Iran fires missiles at Israel
hero.body:
President Trump said he plans to call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discourage him from retaliating for Iran's missile attack on Israel, according to statements the president made to Axios. Trump characterized the recent exchanges as both sides having taken their turn and suggested further escalation was unnecessary.

"I am going to call Bibi right now and tell him not to retaliate. Each of them had their fun. Israel had its strike, and Iran had its strike. We don't need another one," Trump told Axios. The White House confirmed to NewsNation that the president had been informed about the missile launches.

Iran fired multiple waves of ballistic missiles at northern Israel on Sunday night, according to the Israeli Defense Forces. The attack marked Iran's first strike in two months and came after Israel targeted Beirut. The incident put immediate pressure on a fragile ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran.

The missile launches came as the Trump administration works to establish a comprehensive peace agreement to end the conflict. The ceasefire faced early testing from the overnight attack, with Trump now moving quickly to prevent further escalations that could undermine his diplomatic objectives in the Middle East.

Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu flew to Washington for a hastily arranged meeting with Trump, concerned about the direction of nuclear negotiations. Netanyahu worried that Trump's advisers, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, might agree to a deal that only addresses Iran's nuclear program while ignoring ballistic missiles, proxy forces, and human rights issues. Netanyahu planned to present Trump with new intelligence about Iran's military capabilities and long-range missile development.

Iran expressed frustration about Netanyahu's intervention, urging the United States to act independently from Israeli pressure. Ali Larijani, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned American officials not to let Netanyahu's statements shape nuclear negotiations. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stated that America should resist destructive Israeli influences.

The talks between Washington and Tehran began in Oman on Friday, with plans for additional rounds of negotiations. Iran has indicated willingness to dilute its highly enriched uranium stockpile to 60 percent purity, though this remains far above the 3.75 percent limit established under the 2015 nuclear deal. The Iranian government insists on maintaining its right to uranium enrichment for nuclear power plants, a position that could complicate future agreements.

Trump has positioned military assets in the region, deploying the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln and three accompanying warships capable of striking Iranian targets. The United States has also strengthened air defenses at military bases across the Middle East in preparation for potential further escalation.

cards.headline: Ukraine Looks to European Allies as U.S. Steps Back from Peace Mediation
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with leaders from Britain, Germany and France in London to discuss their potential role in peace negotiations with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany and France in London to discuss their potential role as negotiators in peace talks with Russia. The meeting reflects a shift in Ukraine's diplomatic strategy as the United States has stepped back from its mediation efforts.

During the meeting, Zelensky's European allies outlined five conditions for peace talks. The change comes as U.S. President Donald Trump has redirected his focus toward the escalating conflict with Iran, requiring Ukraine to depend more heavily on its European partners for diplomatic support.

cards.headline: Airlines Face $100 Billion Fuel Cost Increase as Iran Conflict Drives Oil Prices Higher
cards.body:
Global airlines are confronting an additional $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year as the ongoing conflict involving Iran continues to disrupt energy markets and drive oil prices sharply higher. The International Air Transport Association estimates that jet fuel prices will be 70 percent higher throughout 2026, forcing carriers to raise ticket prices to offset the financial impact.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March has effectively cut off a critical global oil shipping route, stranding vast quantities of crude and creating severe supply constraints. This disruption has pushed fuel costs to levels not seen in years and represents a significant burden for an industry already operating on thin profit margins.

The fuel crisis has dramatically altered industry forecasts. Iata projects that collective airline profits worldwide will drop roughly in half to $23 billion, down from earlier projections. Some carriers may struggle to survive the shock caused by soaring fuel expenses. Willie Walsh, Iata's director general, stated that "high oil prices will inevitably mean higher ticket prices" and that "there's just no way to avoid that."

Airlines have already begun adjusting fares to recover costs. British Airways chief executive Sean Doyle explained that long-haul and business passengers will likely face the bulk of fare increases, while price-sensitive short-haul holiday flights may be among the last to rise. "If fuel goes up, fares have to go up," Doyle said.

Despite the financial pressure, industry research suggests that roughly half of passengers are prepared to spend substantially more on fares if prices track oil costs. Walsh noted this "bodes well" for a strong northern summer season. Industry data shows that more British and European travelers will fly within the continent than usual, with fewer venturing farther afield given continued uncertainty around Gulf hubs.

Walsh emphasized that while the situation is challenging and margins remain "wafer-thin," concerns about fuel shortages have subsided. He compared the current situation favorably to the Covid crisis, noting that the industry remains profitable and is still forecasting growth, with traffic up 2 percent. However, Walsh acknowledged the predicament facing many carriers, saying the fuel bill increase represents an "existential" threat for some airlines.

Airlines are attempting to manage the crisis through various measures, including optimizing flight routes, adjusting capacity, and negotiating fuel hedging contracts. However, these steps provide only partial relief from the scale of the increase.

The situation remains dependent on developments in the Middle East conflict and whether access to oil shipping routes can be restored. Until the underlying supply disruptions are resolved, the aviation industry expects elevated fuel costs to persist, continuing to pressure both airline profitability and consumer travel expenses.

cards.headline: U.S. Considers Using Frozen Iranian Assets for Gulf Allies' Reconstruction
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department is exploring plans to redirect frozen Iranian assets to help U.S. Gulf allies recover from damages, though Iran has rejected the proposal.
cards.body:
The United States is considering using frozen Iranian assets to pay for damages and reconstruction efforts in Gulf ally nations, according to government sources. The Treasury Department is planning the move as part of efforts to help U.S. Gulf allies recover from recent conflicts.

Iran has rejected the idea of using its assets to pay damages to U.S. allies. The proposal represents another front in the economic pressure campaign against Iran as tensions escalate following the missile exchange with Israel.

cards.headline: Bolton warns Trump's Iran policies could trigger nuclear proliferation
cards.teaser: The former national security adviser wrote that the president's contradictory decisions have created conditions for a regional arms race.
cards.body:
Former national security adviser John Bolton warned Sunday that President Trump's actions in the conflict with Iran could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. Bolton wrote that Trump's approach has created long-term risks for increased nuclear proliferation in the region.

Bolton argued that Trump's often-contradictory decisions during the conflict pose dangers regardless of any future agreement with Iran. The former adviser, who served in the Trump administration before departing over policy disagreements, raised concerns about the administration's Iran strategy.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus Increases Oil Output Quota as Strait of Hormuz Remains Closed
cards.teaser: The oil cartel approved its fourth production quota increase since the Hormuz closure, though the move remains largely symbolic given shipping constraints.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus approved an increase in oil production quotas by 188,000 barrels per day, marking the fourth such increase since the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz. The decision comes as the cartel attempts to address global supply constraints, though the practical impact remains limited while vast quantities of oil remain stranded by the closure of the critical shipping route.

The quota increase represents a largely symbolic gesture given the ongoing conflict in Iran and the continued blockage of the strait, which serves as a vital passage for global oil transport. A ceasefire in the region remains elusive, leaving the production increase unable to address the underlying supply crisis that has driven oil prices sharply higher.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping to Visit North Korea
cards.teaser: Beijing is working to reassert influence over North Korea as the strategically important but unpredictable partnership faces new pressures.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping plans to travel to North Korea in a move analysts say is designed to strengthen Beijing's influence over its neighbor. The visit comes as China seeks to maintain its role with a strategically vital partner whose actions remain difficult to predict.

The trip represents China's effort to balance its relationship with North Korea amid shifting regional dynamics. Beijing views the relationship as important to its broader strategic interests in Northeast Asia, even as North Korea's actions sometimes complicate Chinese diplomacy.

hero.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with leaders from Britain, Germany and France in London to discuss their potential role in peace negotiations with Russia.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany and France in London to discuss their potential role as negotiators in peace talks with Russia. The meeting reflects a shift in Ukraine's diplomatic strategy as the United States has stepped back from its mediation efforts.

During the meeting, Zelensky's European allies outlined five conditions for peace talks. The change comes as U.S. President Donald Trump has redirected his focus toward the escalating conflict with Iran, requiring Ukraine to depend more heavily on its European partners for diplomatic support.

cards.headline: Political Rift Divides Senegal's President and Prime Minister
cards.teaser: Two leaders who together defeated Senegal's political old guard are now fighting each other in a bitter dispute.
cards.body:
Senegal's president and prime minister, who campaigned together to defeat the country's entrenched political establishment, are now in conflict with each other. Their partnership has fractured since taking power.

The dispute threatens stability in Senegal, a West African nation long regarded as a democratic model in the region. The disagreement between the two leaders has created uncertainty about the country's political future.

cards.headline: Economic Crisis Deepens Despair Among Iranians
cards.teaser: Skyrocketing inflation and an imploding economy are causing hopelessness across Iranian society as the country faces mounting pressures.
cards.body:
Iran's economy continues to deteriorate, with skyrocketing inflation causing widespread despair among both pro-government and anti-government Iranians. The economic collapse is affecting citizens across political divides as basic necessities become increasingly unaffordable.

For those who had hoped for regime change, the economic crisis has brought particular disappointment. The combination of war deaths and economic hardship is creating a sense of hopelessness throughout Iranian society as living conditions worsen.

cards.headline: Israeli Gunman Kills One in Central Israel Attack
cards.teaser: An Arab citizen of Israel carried out a shooting attack that left one person dead before the assailant was killed.
cards.body:
A gunman who was an Arab citizen of Israel killed one person in an attack in central Israel before being killed himself. Hamas praised the shooting but did not claim responsibility for the attack.

The attack comes amid heightened regional tensions following the exchange of fire between Israel and Iran. The incident adds to security concerns within Israel as the country navigates multiple fronts of conflict.

cards.headline: Rights Defender Works to Protect Ukrainian Soldiers from Command Abuses
cards.teaser: A Ukrainian advocate focuses on protecting soldiers from mistreatment by their own commanders rather than threats from Russian forces.
cards.body:
Ukraine has established a rights defender position dedicated to protecting the country's soldiers from abuses by their own military commanders. The role focuses on addressing internal military misconduct rather than external threats from Russia.

The position reflects concerns about treatment of Ukrainian fighters within their own command structure. The defender works to document and address cases where soldiers face problems from their leadership as the war continues.

hero.headline: FBI arrests three men on charges of plotting to support ISIS
hero.body:
Federal authorities arrested three men in separate locations across the United States on charges of plotting to support the Islamic State terror group. The FBI took into custody a 25-year-old man in Lakeside, California, a suspect in Leawood, Kansas, and a third individual, according to multiple reports. The arrests represent a coordinated operation targeting alleged domestic supporters of ISIS.

According to court documents cited by The Jerusalem Post, one of the suspects allegedly expressed extreme anti-American sentiments, stating he wished he could kill 300 million Americans. The men are accused of planning to provide material support to ISIS, including funding for weapons that would be used in terrorist attacks against Americans. The specific nature of their alleged plotting and whether the suspects knew each other was not disclosed in available reports.

The investigation was conducted by the FBI, which has maintained focus on identifying individuals in the United States who may seek to provide support to foreign terrorist organizations. ISIS, also known as the Islamic State, has faced military defeat in its former territorial holdings in Iraq and Syria but continues to inspire attacks and recruit supporters globally. The terror group has been responsible for mass casualties in the Middle East and has inspired or directed attacks in Western countries.

The arrests come at a time when national security officials have warned about the persistent threat of homegrown extremism. While ISIS lost its physical caliphate years ago, law enforcement agencies continue to monitor online spaces where the group's propaganda circulates and where potential supporters may be radicalized. The FBI has disrupted numerous plots in recent years involving individuals allegedly seeking to carry out attacks in the name of ISIS or travel overseas to join the organization.

All three suspects are expected to face federal charges related to providing material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization, a crime that carries substantial prison time. The cases will likely be prosecuted in federal courts in the districts where the arrests took place. The FBI has not released additional details about the timeline of the alleged plotting or whether the men posed an imminent threat at the time of their arrests.

cards.headline: Trump ends NBC interview after dispute over election fraud claims
cards.teaser: The former president walked out of a Meet the Press taping when pressed on past statements about the 2020 election.
cards.body:
Donald Trump abruptly ended an NBC "Meet the Press" interview after being challenged by host Kristen Welker over his claims that the 2020 election was rigged. The 79-year-old former president walked out before the taping was completed.

Trump clashed with Welker when she repeatedly questioned him on several points during the interview, including his false assertions about election fraud.

cards.headline: Israel strikes Beirut suburbs after Hezbollah drone attack
cards.teaser: The Israeli military launched retaliatory strikes on Hezbollah positions following a drone assault on Israeli forces.
cards.body:
Israel conducted retaliatory airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs after Hezbollah launched fighter drones at Israeli military targets, according to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office. Israeli officials stated the attacks were ordered in direct response to Hezbollah's firing at Israeli territory.

The strikes represent the latest escalation in ongoing hostilities between Israel and the Lebanese militant group, continuing a cycle of tit-for-tat attacks amid broader regional tensions.

cards.headline: Australian melanoma doctor dies after experimental brain tumor treatment
cards.teaser: A physician who underwent a pioneering cancer treatment has died, though the research has generated optimism for future therapies.
cards.body:
Prof Richard Scolyer, a world-renowned melanoma researcher and former Australian of the Year, has died at age 59. The pathologist was diagnosed with inoperable brain cancer in 2023 and chose to undergo an experimental treatment approach. Scolyer was known for his pioneering work in cancer immunotherapy.

His family released a statement he had prepared before his final illness. Despite the outcome, his case has drawn attention within the medical community for the novel nature of the experimental treatment he received.

cards.headline: Urban birds alter songs to compete with traffic noise
cards.teaser: Researchers found that some city-dwelling bird species are modifying their vocalizations to be heard over urban sounds.
cards.body:
Scientists at the Centre for Ecological Research in Hungary have found that some city-dwelling birds are changing their songs in response to urban noise. Traffic and other sounds from human activity create acoustic challenges that interfere with how birds communicate, defend territories, and attract mates.

The research demonstrates how wildlife adapts to survive in human-dominated environments. As cities continue to expand, birds are among the species modifying their behavior to cope with the noise pollution that comes with urban life.

cards.headline: Justice Department refutes vote count claims in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: Federal officials debunked social media allegations about discrepancies in vote tallies for candidate Spencer Pratt.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice dismissed viral social media claims alleging voting irregularities in the Los Angeles mayoral election. The false allegations centered on reality television personality Spencer Pratt, who ran for mayor, with some posts claiming he received zero votes in certain tallies.

The Los Angeles Daily News confirmed that the vote count claim stemmed from a misreading of data. CNBC reported that data misinterpretation fueled the false allegations that spread across social platforms. Democracy Docket and CNN both reported on the DOJ's debunking of the claims.

cards.headline: BBC investigation exposes illegal sperm donor services targeting vulnerable women
cards.teaser: An undercover probe found unregulated donors selling sperm through social media platforms.
cards.body:
A BBC investigation uncovered illegal sperm donor operations targeting vulnerable women through social media. Undercover reporters purchased sperm from an unregulated donor for £100, which was delivered by post alongside a carton of passata.

The investigation revealed that donors are bypassing licensed fertility clinics to offer sperm directly to women online. This practice circumvents legal requirements that fertility services screen donors for infectious diseases and maintain proper records.

cards.headline: Stock Futures Drop Following Nasdaq Decline as Markets Digest Jobs Report
cards.teaser: Stock futures fell after the Nasdaq suffered its worst day of the year, with rising odds of Federal Reserve interest rate increases weighing on markets.
cards.body:
US employers added 172,000 jobs in May while the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.3%, signaling a resilient labor market despite inflation concerns and Middle East tensions. However, the positive jobs data triggered a sharp stock market selloff on Friday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq closing down 4%—its largest single-day drop in over a year. The S&P 500 fell 2.6% and the Dow declined 1.3%.

The market decline reflected investor concerns that strong employment data could prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain higher interest rates for longer. Technology and artificial intelligence stocks experienced particularly heavy selling pressure, driving the broader market downturn.

cards.headline: Trump Criticizes Potential Fed Rate Increases Ahead of New Chair's First Week
cards.teaser: Former President Donald Trump called for interest rate cuts and said raising rates would be wrong, adding pressure on incoming Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh.
cards.body:
Donald Trump has publicly criticized the possibility of Federal Reserve interest rate increases, arguing there is no reason to raise rates following the latest jobs report. His comments come as Kevin Warsh prepares to begin his tenure as the new Federal Reserve chair, adding pressure on him ahead of his first policy decisions.

Markets fell sharply after strong employment data increased expectations for rate increases to combat potential inflation. Financial analysts have warned that markets are entering a warning zone given the conflicting pressures between robust employment figures and the administration's preference for lower rates.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly Diabetes Drug Shows Significant Weight Loss and Sleep Apnea Benefits
cards.teaser: A new triple-action diabetes medication from Eli Lilly reduced blood sugar and body weight while improving sleep apnea and knee pain in clinical trials.
cards.body:
Eli Lilly's retatrutide, a triple-action weekly injection for type 2 diabetes, demonstrated substantial results in phase 3 clinical trials. Patients receiving the drug for 40 weeks lost more than four times as much weight as those on placebo, while their long-term blood sugar levels dropped more than twice as much.

The medication works by mimicking three gut hormones—GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon—to control appetite, blood sugar, and metabolism. Unlike existing treatments such as Ozempic or Mounjaro, retatrutide's inclusion of glucagon receptor engagement helps increase energy expenditure, offering a more comprehensive approach to managing type 2 diabetes and obesity.

cards.headline: Marks and Spencer Launches Training Program for 1,000 Young People
cards.teaser: The British retailer introduced a new traineeship scheme aimed at helping young people who are not in employment, education, or training.
cards.body:
Marks and Spencer has launched a new traineeship program for 1,000 young people. The scheme is designed to address what the retailer identifies as a growing challenge: the number of young people not in employment, education, or training.

The initiative represents M&S's commitment to tackling youth unemployment and supporting skills development in the retail sector.

cards.headline: Horror Spoof Film Opens With $55 Million, Largest R-Rated Comedy Debut in 12 Years
cards.teaser: The latest Scary Movie installment took in $55 million at the box office, marking the biggest opening for an R-rated comedy since 2014.
cards.body:
The sixth installment of the Scary Movie franchise earned $55 million during its opening weekend at the U.S. and Canadian box office, marking the largest debut for an R-rated comedy in 12 years.

The film's strong performance reflects the ongoing appeal of horror spoofs alongside the current popularity of horror films. The Scary Movie series has historically relied on timing its releases to capitalize on trends in the genre it parodies.

hero.headline: NASA partners with Prada for Artemis IV spacesuits
hero.body:
NASA is collaborating with luxury fashion house Prada to develop specialized undergarments for astronauts on the Artemis IV moon mission scheduled for 2028. The partnership focuses on creating a Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG) that astronauts will wear as a base layer beneath their spacesuits during lunar surface operations.

The LCVG represents Prada's contribution to the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit project. This undergarment serves a critical function in managing astronaut body temperature during moon exploration, where surface conditions present extreme thermal challenges. The lunar environment experiences dramatic temperature swings, from intense heat in direct sunlight to severe cold in shadowed areas, requiring advanced thermal management systems.

Prada's involvement demonstrates the luxury brand's expansion into the space industry through technical engineering applications. The company has applied its materials science expertise to develop specialized fabrics and thermal regulation technology for the LCVG. This collaboration reflects a broader trend of luxury brands pursuing innovation beyond traditional fashion into specialized technical fields.

NASA has increasingly pursued partnerships with private sector companies to accelerate development of next-generation space equipment. The Artemis program represents a significant part of this strategy, with the agency leveraging commercial innovation to support its lunar exploration goals. The Artemis IV mission is part of the broader effort to establish sustained human presence on the moon.

Previous Apollo-era spacesuits used simpler thermal control systems that constrained the duration and scope of moonwalk activities. The new Prada-designed LCVG addresses these historical limitations by providing both cooling and insulation capabilities needed for extended surface operations. The garment's sophisticated temperature management system will allow astronauts greater flexibility during their time on the lunar surface.

The Prada-designed components will undergo extensive testing before deployment on Artemis IV. NASA continues to develop multiple aspects of its lunar exploration equipment through commercial partnerships, reflecting a strategic approach to space exploration that combines government expertise with private sector innovation.

The Artemis IV mission builds on earlier Artemis flights. Artemis II, currently facing scheduling adjustments due to technical issues with the Space Launch System rocket, will conduct a crewed lunar flyby in 2025. That mission will carry four astronauts, including Americans Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen, on a 10-day trip around the moon that will set new distance records for human spaceflight.

Artemis III, planned for 2028, will achieve the first human moon landing since the Apollo program's final flight in 1972. The Artemis IV mission will follow, continuing NASA's goal of establishing long-term lunar operations. Through partnerships like the one with Prada, NASA aims to ensure that astronauts have access to cutting-edge equipment designed for the demands of deep-space exploration.

cards.headline: Notion restores Anthropic AI access after outage
cards.teaser: Notion's productivity platform restored access to Anthropic's AI features following a service disruption that affected users.
cards.body:
Notion resolved a service disruption that had cut off user access to Anthropic AI features integrated into its productivity platform. The company restored full functionality to the AI-powered tools that many users rely on for document creation and organization tasks.

Notion's head of product commented on the significant user response to the outage, noting the high volume of social media reactions. The disruption highlighted how central AI features have become to the platform's daily operations for many Notion users.

cards.headline: Australian Aboriginal stories may preserve 10,000-year-old coastal memories
cards.teaser: Researchers propose that some Aboriginal oral traditions may remember coastlines that disappeared underwater over 10,000 years ago.
cards.body:
Some Australian Aboriginal stories appear to contain memories of coastlines that vanished beneath rising seas more than 10,000 years ago, according to researchers studying oral traditions. The stories could represent some of humanity's oldest surviving accurate narratives passed down through generations.

The research suggests these oral histories preserve geographic details of landscapes that existed during the last ice age, when sea levels were significantly lower than today. The findings add to understanding of how oral traditions can maintain factual information across thousands of years through careful cultural transmission.

cards.headline: Persona 6 revealed at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: Atlus announced Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase, confirming earlier leaks about the game's development.
cards.body:
Atlus officially announced Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase at Summer Game Fest 2026, confirming the long-awaited return of the beloved role-playing series. The announcement came alongside other major Japanese RPG reveals at the event, including the conclusion of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy.

The studio shared only a brief teaser for the game, keeping most details under wraps. Persona 6 marks the next numbered entry in a franchise known for blending high school life simulation with supernatural combat mechanics.

cards.headline: Sega confirms generative AI used in Crazy Taxi reboot
cards.teaser: Sega acknowledged using generative AI content in its upcoming Crazy Taxi: World Tour game, scheduled for 2027.
cards.body:
Sega confirmed that generative AI technology was used in development of Crazy Taxi: World Tour, the series reboot set for release in 2027. The company responded to questions about AI-generated content after it was identified in promotional materials for the game.

Crazy Taxi: World Tour marks the return of the arcade racing franchise after a long hiatus. The original Crazy Taxi gained popularity in arcades and on home consoles for its fast-paced driving gameplay and urban environments. The new entry will release on Xbox and other platforms.

cards.headline: Microsoft releases translucent green Xbox for 25th anniversary
cards.teaser: Microsoft unveiled a limited edition translucent green Xbox Series X console celebrating the brand's 25th anniversary.
cards.body:
Microsoft unveiled a special edition Xbox Series X in translucent green to celebrate the brand's 25th anniversary. The design draws inspiration from the original Xbox console, featuring a transparent green aesthetic on both the console and matching controller—marking the first time Xbox Series X has received a translucent design treatment.

The anniversary console was revealed at Xbox Showcase 2026. The limited edition hardware represents Microsoft's nostalgic callback to gaming aesthetics from earlier Xbox generations.

cards.headline: Halo: Campaign Evolved launches July 28 with space combat
cards.teaser: Halo: Campaign Evolved will release on July 28 across multiple platforms, introducing new space combat missions to the series.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced that Halo: Campaign Evolved will release on July 28 across Xbox Series S/X, PC, and PS5, with pre-orders now available. The remake of Halo: Combat Evolved's campaign was revealed during Xbox Games Showcase, featuring a new mission trailer showcasing Operation: Meteorite, a three-mission space combat experience.

The remake expands the original game with new mission types, introducing space combat gameplay alongside the traditional ground-based first-person shooter action the franchise is known for.

hero.headline: Alexander Zverev wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first Grand Slam title on Sunday, defeating Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in a tense five-set final at the French Open. The second-seeded German dropped to his back and began crying after Cobolli missed an overhead on the second championship point.

The victory comes after three previous Grand Slam final losses. Zverev had won at nearly every other level of professional tennis, including Masters 1000 events, two ATP Finals titles, and an Olympic gold medal in Tokyo in 2020, but the sport's biggest prize had eluded him until now.

The tournament itself proved chaotic, with top seed Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic bouncing out in consecutive days, while Carlos Alcaraz remained absent due to injury. This left Zverev as the strongest player remaining in the draw.

Cobolli, ranked number 14 in the world, reached his first Grand Slam final without playing a semifinal match after his Italian compatriot Matteo Arnaldi withdrew due to illness. The 22-year-old felt the occasion intensely from the start, playing poorly in the opening set as Zverev dominated 6-1.

Cobolli regrouped in the second set, improving his forehand and using his drop shot effectively. Zverev's familiar vulnerabilities emerged, including problems with his forehand and second serve. The German made two double faults at 3-3 and committed unforced errors on break point, allowing Cobolli to level the match.

Zverev reasserted control in the third set, particularly through his serving. He broke Cobolli at 5-4 when the Italian sprayed three wild errors from 30-0 up. Yet as the finish line approached, Zverev's nerves took hold. He appeared overwhelmed throughout much of the fourth set, though Cobolli also struggled. In a tiebreak, Cobolli mounted a comeback from 3-1 down, winning with a running forehand winner to force a fifth set.

However, the Italian's energy reserves had been depleted. Cobolli completely faltered at the start of the fifth set, losing his opening service game and never recovering.

After the match, Zverev addressed his team, saying: "We've been through injuries. We've been through heartbreak. We've been through losses. We've been losers at times in the important moments. But at the end of the day, we're grand slam champions now and that's what counts."

Zverev also reflected on his personal connection to Roland Garros, mentioning both his greatest moments and his lowest point on the court. He noted overcoming a serious injury, adding: "I had the worst moment of my life on this court. I was laying in that corner over there with seven broken ligaments and two fractured bones. But now, finally, it's a happy end."

cards.headline: Stacey King, three-time NBA champion with Bulls, dies at 59
cards.teaser: The former player who became a fan favorite broadcaster has died.
cards.body:
Stacey King, a three-time NBA champion with the Chicago Bulls, has died at age 59. King won his championships with the Bulls during their dominant period in the 1990s.

Following his playing career, King became a fan favorite as a member of the Bulls broadcast team, where he provided commentary and analysis for the franchise.

cards.headline: Spurs remain confident despite 2-0 NBA Finals deficit
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama and San Antonio head to Madison Square Garden facing elimination pressure.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs are embracing their challenge as they prepare for Game 3 of the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks on Monday night at Madison Square Garden. The Spurs trail 2-0 in the best-of-seven series.

Wembanyama acknowledged the difficult circumstances but emphasized acceptance and perspective. "I think the key is acceptance a lot of times, taking a step back, realizing all the journey that's behind this and what's ahead of this," he said. The star player is approaching the setback as part of his first NBA playoff run.

cards.headline: Knicks aim to maintain focus ahead of first Finals home game in 27 years
cards.teaser: New York prepares for Game 3 at Madison Square Garden amid intense media attention.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

The New York Knicks are working to stay focused on basketball as Madison Square Garden prepares to host its first NBA Finals game since June 25, 1999. If the atmosphere surrounding Game 3 is any indication of Monday night's environment, players expect a chaotic scene at the arena.

Knicks players say they are doing their best to block out the surrounding hoopla and concentrate on the task at hand. The team holds a 2-0 lead over the San Antonio Spurs heading into the home game, putting them in position to take a commanding series advantage.

---

Note: The provided source material is about Duffy's concert return and a straight-to-VHS film release—neither relates to the Knicks NBA Finals story. Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Christian Eriksen conscious after collapsing during Denmark match
cards.teaser: A friendly between Denmark and Ukraine was called off after the medical emergency.
cards.body:
Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen collapsed during a friendly match against Ukraine. The Danish Football Association confirmed that Eriksen was conscious following the incident.

The medical emergency led to the abandonment of the friendly match, with player welfare taking priority over completing the game.

cards.headline: NYPD cancels Madison Square Garden watch party for NBA Finals Game 3
cards.teaser: Enhanced security measures for President Trump's attendance prompted the change.
cards.body:
The New York Police Department has canceled the outdoor watch party scheduled for Game 3 of the NBA Finals outside Madison Square Garden on Monday night. The decision was made following discussions between the Secret Service and NYPD due to President Donald Trump's planned attendance at the game.

The Knicks are implementing enhanced security measures for the event, asking fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff and bring minimal belongings. The watch party cancellation comes after more than 20 arrests occurred at a similar outdoor gathering following Game 2 on Friday.

cards.headline: Hurricanes coach noncommittal on Game 4 lineup changes
cards.teaser: Rod Brind'Amour says he does not anticipate major adjustments after falling behind in Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Carolina Hurricanes coach Rod Brind'Amour said he does not anticipate a lot of changes to his Game 4 lineup following his team's loss that put them behind 2-1 in the Stanley Cup Final series against the Vegas Golden Knights. Brind'Amour declined to specify whether he would make a goaltender change.

The Hurricanes now trail in the best-of-seven series after dropping Game 3. Brind'Amour's comments suggest he plans to largely stick with the roster that brought Carolina to the Finals, though he left open the possibility of minor adjustments heading into the next game.

hero.headline: 79th Tony Awards Underway as Broadway Season Concludes Without Clear Frontrunners
hero.body:
The 79th Tony Awards ceremony began Sunday evening, marking the culmination of a record Broadway season with no dominant production heading into theater's biggest night. "The Lost Boys," a punk-rock adaptation of the 1987 cult horror film featuring high-flying vampires, and "Schmigadoon!," a comedic tribute to Golden Age musicals, each entered the ceremony with 12 nominations, the most of any productions this year.

The awards ceremony kicked off at 8 p.m. ET with stars arriving on the red carpet throughout the evening. The competitive field reflects a diverse Broadway season that saw productions ranging from updated classics to original works compete for recognition across multiple categories.

Broadway's 2025-2026 season set records for attendance and box office revenue, contributing to the heightened anticipation surrounding this year's awards. The ceremony will recognize excellence across categories including best musical, best play, acting performances, and technical achievements. The variety of nominated works spans multiple genres and theatrical styles, from the supernatural storytelling of "The Lost Boys" to the nostalgic musical comedy of "Schmigadoon!"

Other notable contenders include productions exploring themes from American literature to contemporary social movements, though none have emerged as the presumptive winner heading into the ceremony. The awards will be presented throughout the evening, with winners announced across all major categories.

The ceremony represents the theater industry's annual celebration of artistic achievement and commercial success on Broadway. With no single production dominating the nominations or pre-ceremony predictions, the evening promises a competitive field across multiple categories. The results will be updated throughout the night as winners are announced in each category.

cards.headline: Lawsuit Filed to Block UFC Fight Planned for White House South Lawn
cards.teaser: Two Virginia residents have filed suit against federal agencies to stop a UFC event scheduled at the White House as part of the nation's 250th birthday celebration.
cards.body:
Two Virginia residents filed a federal lawsuit Saturday to stop a UFC event scheduled for the White House South Lawn. The fight card, called UFC Freedom 250, is being held as part of America's 250th anniversary celebration and coincides with President Trump's 80th birthday.

The plaintiffs are challenging the National Park Service and the Department of the Interior, the federal agencies overseeing the White House grounds. The lawsuit seeks to prevent the mixed martial arts spectacle from taking place at the presidential residence.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Addresses Bari Weiss Era at CBS News in Public Comments
cards.teaser: The veteran CBS correspondent discussed the current state of CBS News and called for the removal of Bari Weiss during recent public statements.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, recently dismissed from CBS News, has accused editor-in-chief Bari Weiss of editorial interference in a 60 Minutes segment about the death of Minneapolis protester Renee Good, who was killed by an immigration officer in January. Pelley claimed Weiss sent an email requesting changes to the report before it aired, alleging she wanted the segment to state that Good was driving toward an officer—language that echoed Trump's characterization of the incident.

The controversy has drawn attention from industry figures, including Sarah Safer, daughter of longtime 60 Minutes correspondent Morley Safer. She criticized the changes at CBS News under Weiss's leadership, expressing concern about threats to journalistic independence. Meanwhile, several other veteran correspondents including Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim have indicated they plan to continue with the program.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Opens Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland
cards.teaser: The singer performed the first show of her Eternal Sunshine Tour at Oakland Arena on Saturday night.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande opened her Eternal Sunshine Tour with a performance at Oakland Arena on Saturday night. The show drew praise for Grande's vocal abilities and the ambitious scale of the production.

The tour is named after Grande's recent album and features material from that project alongside a full concert production with staging and setlists built around the new music.

cards.headline: New Spyro Game Announced for Spring 2027 Release
cards.teaser: Toys for Bob and Microsoft's Activision revealed the first new Spyro game in nearly two decades, titled "Spyro: A Real Beyond."
cards.body:
Toys for Bob has unveiled "Spyro: A Realm Beyond," the first original Spyro game in nearly two decades. The California-based studio announced the title at Xbox Game Showcase, with the purple dragon set to launch in spring 2027 across Xbox, PlayStation 5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.

Tom Kenny, who voiced Spyro in the original 1990s PlayStation games, returns for the new adventure. A major gameplay innovation lets players take flight at any time, allowing them to dive for speed, breathe fire to create updrafts, and flap their wings—fully embracing the capabilities of being a dragon.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Cancels Pittsburgh Concert Over Weather Forecast
cards.teaser: The country singer canceled a Pittsburgh performance citing safety concerns about adverse weather conditions that ultimately did not materialize.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled his Pittsburgh concert due to a forecasted severe weather event that ultimately did not materialize as predicted. The singer defended his decision by citing safety concerns related to his large stage setup, which he said could pose a fatal risk to attendees in adverse conditions.

Wallen addressed criticism over the cancelation, characterizing some of the surrounding commentary as "nonsense." His statement emphasized that the decision prioritized fan safety, even though the anticipated dangerous weather did not arrive as originally forecasted.

cards.headline: Bob Dylan Performs Basement Tapes Song for First Time in 14 Years
cards.teaser: Dylan played "You Ain't Goin' Nowhere" during a recent performance, marking the first time he has performed the song since 2012.
cards.body:
Bob Dylan recently played "You Ain't Goin' Nowhere" in concert, marking the first time in 14 years he's performed this Basement Tapes track. The song comes from Dylan's late 1960s Basement Tapes sessions.

Two days before this performance, Dylan also debuted "Baby, Won't You Be My Baby" live—59 years after originally recording it. These back-to-back performances of deep cuts from the Basement Tapes era represent notably rare setlist selections for the legendary artist.

hero.headline: Trump tells Netanyahu not to retaliate after Iran fires missiles at Israel
hero.body:
President Trump said he plans to call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discourage him from retaliating for Iran's missile attack on Israel, according to statements the president made to Axios. Trump characterized the recent exchanges as both sides having taken their turn and suggested further escalation was unnecessary.

"I am going to call Bibi right now and tell him not to retaliate. Each of them had their fun. Israel had its strike, and Iran had its strike. We don't need another one," Trump told Axios. The White House confirmed to NewsNation that the president had been informed about the missile launches.

Iran fired multiple waves of ballistic missiles at northern Israel on Sunday night, according to the Israeli Defense Forces. The attack marked Iran's first strike in two months and came after Israel targeted Beirut. The incident put immediate pressure on a fragile ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran.

The missile launches came as the Trump administration works to establish a comprehensive peace agreement to end the conflict. The ceasefire faced early testing from the overnight attack, with Trump now moving quickly to prevent further escalations that could undermine his diplomatic objectives in the Middle East.

Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu flew to Washington for a hastily arranged meeting with Trump, concerned about the direction of nuclear negotiations. Netanyahu worried that Trump's advisers, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, might agree to a deal that only addresses Iran's nuclear program while ignoring ballistic missiles, proxy forces, and human rights issues. Netanyahu planned to present Trump with new intelligence about Iran's military capabilities and long-range missile development.

Iran expressed frustration about Netanyahu's intervention, urging the United States to act independently from Israeli pressure. Ali Larijani, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned American officials not to let Netanyahu's statements shape nuclear negotiations. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stated that America should resist destructive Israeli influences.

The talks between Washington and Tehran began in Oman on Friday, with plans for additional rounds of negotiations. Iran has indicated willingness to dilute its highly enriched uranium stockpile to 60 percent purity, though this remains far above the 3.75 percent limit established under the 2015 nuclear deal. The Iranian government insists on maintaining its right to uranium enrichment for nuclear power plants, a position that could complicate future agreements.

Trump has positioned military assets in the region, deploying the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln and three accompanying warships capable of striking Iranian targets. The United States has also strengthened air defenses at military bases across the Middle East in preparation for potential further escalation.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges UFC fight planned for White House South Lawn
cards.teaser: A legal filing contends the Trump administration unlawfully authorized a UFC event scheduled for the president's birthday.
cards.body:
A federal lawsuit seeks to halt a UFC fight card scheduled for the White House South Lawn on June 14, coinciding with President Trump's 80th birthday and part of celebrations marking the nation's 250th anniversary.

The legal filing challenges whether the Trump administration had the authority to authorize a commercial mixed martial arts competition on White House grounds, arguing the decision violated the law.

cards.headline: Maine Democrats consider Electoral College changes if Nebraska alters system
cards.teaser: Democratic gubernatorial candidates in Maine have signaled support for adopting a winner-take-all electoral vote system if Nebraska makes similar changes.
cards.body:
Democrats in Maine are threatening to change how the state awards Electoral College votes if Republican-led Nebraska modifies its system for the 2028 presidential election. Several Democrats running to be Maine's next governor have indicated they would support adopting a winner-take-all approach if Nebraska abandons its current method.

The potential changes represent the latest example of partisan electoral politics that could influence the outcome of the 2028 White House race. Both Maine and Nebraska currently split their electoral votes, unlike the winner-take-all systems used by most other states.

cards.headline: House Democrats plan investigations of Trump administration officials
cards.teaser: Democratic lawmakers are preparing to examine alleged legal violations by Trump officials across immigration enforcement, financial practices, and prosecutorial decisions.
cards.body:
House Democrats want 2029 to mark a year of accountability for Trump administration officials, with plans for investigations and possible prosecutions. Democrats have accused top members of Trump's team of violating laws across multiple areas, including deadly immigration raids, strikes on alleged drug boats, financial conflicts of interest, and targeting the president's political enemies for prosecution.

The Department of Justice would play a central role in any potential prosecutions stemming from Democratic investigations. The planned scrutiny covers a wide range of activities by Trump administration officials over the course of the president's second term.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in the general election.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary under President Biden, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Her victory sets up a general election race where she could make history.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history. She previously served as a U.S. representative from New Mexico before joining the Biden administration.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead California governor primary as votes are counted
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra vie for nominations to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California's governor primary results show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra leading their respective party contests. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer also competed for their party's nomination, while Republican Chad Bianco ran alongside Hilton.

The nominees will compete to replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who is term-limited. Vote counting continues as the state tallies ballots from the primary election.

cards.headline: Raman closes gap with Pratt in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: City Councilmember Nithya Raman now trails Republican Spencer Pratt by two percentage points in the contest for Los Angeles mayor.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilmember Nithya Raman has narrowed the margin in the city's mayoral race, closing to within two points of Republican Spencer Pratt, according to Decision Desk HQ. As of Sunday evening, Raman stood in third place with 26.21 percent of the vote behind Pratt and current Mayor Karen Bass.

Raman, a Democrat, has gained ground as additional ballots were counted. Pratt, a former reality television star, leads the field of candidates competing to become the city's next mayor.
